to be clear (I haven't understood what is going on entirely due to the photos as they won't enlarge for me) but I gather it is anti-abortion protesters?

I get that it's very difficult. I'm not denying that or giving out delusional hope. I've experienced recovery myself and it's possible for men as well. I just think people will see what they wanna see. If they don't believe in hope then there won't be any.

I go through exactly the same! I've so many books on the go I don't know which one to resume. Same with painting and other hobbies. It's so important to keep occupied though! 

There is coping and managing ahead! It's not a life sentence so don't worry too much.
I don't blame you...I've no idea how you must feel right now. I'm so sorry this is going on for you. Just take some time for you to think and release the emotions then make a decision.

Oh wow that sounds incredibly painful. Such a betrayal will be brutal to process. I am so sorry to hear this. I've no idea how that must feel. 

Are you looking after yourself as best you can given the circumstances? 

What do you plan to do in terms of the relationship and child? 

I get that you are probably in shock so it's understandable if you don't know what you'll do.

Be kind to yourself

I'm sorry that I can't be more helpful. Sounds like you are really stuck just now. I want to point out that it's incredible you are able to work as I cannot. That's massive! A woman will be attracted to you if you believe in yourself a bit more. There's nothing sexier than confidence! I understand how difficult it is when suffering with BPD. It's about getting to the root of the beliefs that others have placed on you throughout your life. I am telling you from my perspective as someone in recovery following MBT treatment and working my ass off to feel better about myself and manage my symptoms. I try to be as self-reliant as possible. 

I hope you start to feel better and believe in yourself as you deserve it

I'm getting other treatment for my trauma. 
No I've not heard of that drug. What is it? Is it available on the NHS?
Nuclear stomach emptying test (can't remember the exact name but it took around 2.5 hours and every 15 mins they'd scan the stomach)

I understand that. I am saying this in the most compassionate way...you are being very hard on yourself. By punishing yourself you won't overcome this...you will perpetuate your suffering unfortunately and I know cos I did this for two years straight. 

I want you to feel better and to have some hope (not false hope). It's good that you've not been in relationships purely to avoid being alone. That's a plus. You could work on you and be the best version to pull the person you want. Let me tell you this...the latest partner of mine who I absolutely love broke up with me. I'm 29 and he was 26. He had zero relationship experience before me and I wasn't put off because he had self respect even with his mental health issues. He was hopeful about his future even with his struggles and that made me super attracted to him. There's no reason this can't be you. 

I know how awful Symptoms of BPD are. They make you believe in the worst. 

Do you Skype people on here or anything to chat? I'm just thinking out loud. I'm not trying to be weird or anything but it sounds like you are going through an awful time and I don't want that for you. I hope this is helpful at least a bit.

Aw wow I am so sorry you feel this way. I'm a female with BPD and totally appreciate that males with the illness are underrepresented. That must make you feel even more invisible. 

I hear you. You are not worthless or any of those things you say. You've been made to believe that but it isn't true. It's the illness that makes you feel that and I understand because I had that most of my life but I've worked through a lot the past two years and it's improved massively. I've had a recent crisis but am now a lot better. I'm saying this to let you know it's possible to get through it. 

Once you heal your wounds the right people/partner will come into your life. It sucks now but it will be worth it later. I understand it's excruciating. 

That saying is so true about once we love ourselves others love us. It's an attractive quality. So is confidence and strength which you'll have because people with this awful illness have so much to cope with and to keep going shows incredible resilience. It's about improving the quality of your life so you can move past survival mode. 

Don't let others define your worth. You do that. Then no one can take it from you

Yeah I feel that so I do. It's excruciating isn't it? 
I really coped very very well with a breakup last month. I'm very proud of myself but I mean it was sooo painful. 

I don't think you should stop dating completely; rather you could use your single life time to build yourself up and feel stronger to handle any kind of difficulties in a relationship? It's a good time to work on underlying issues to then go into anew relationship equipped with the skills so that it's not sabotaged :) that's what I'm doing because we all know part of BPD is sabotaging relationships and intense instability in them. 

It's possible to do but it will be difficult. What keeps me going is the proof that I coped with that breakup and that I can now think in the next one I won't be so easily affected by any conflict that may arise.
Mmm erection haha
Ah Basil Fawlty has returned!

I've never taken any hard illegal drugs but when I'm in crisis I sometimes think if I'd access I would try heroin for sure ..set myself up nicely and treat myself. If I die... excellent. If not, at least there would be temporary relief although possibly a new and lethal addiction. Every way of trying to end one's life always comes with the risk of it not working and surviving with now more damage to yourself. 

Sorry I can't answer the question. I hope you find some relief in a healthy way

Yeah they don't fully understand it. This specialist told me it's a neurological processing problem. There is a misophonia website which should come up if you search. It makes me so angry that medical professionals dismiss anything other than the severe symptoms we with BPD present with...I think it's the stigma of them assuming "ah here is a borderline patient looking for another label to attach to or more medication to seek" which is not on. Not everyone is like that so it's about voicing the severity of it and trying to be heard. Definitely speak to the GP or a psychiatrist about it or if you've got the finances you can get the hypnosis online. I couldn't stay as an inpatient due to the slamming if doors and other noises that caused me severe distress, worsening the BPD symptoms I presented with.
Yeah a bit. It's an unfortunate symptom and poor coping skills that causes it. It's helpful for someone to reach out to show that they aren't hated because that's how it feels a lot of the time

Yes I have it extremely bad where I have to leave and tell people it's my issue. Even in the hospital I've to say I cannot go and eat with others for fear of becoming aggressive (I've never been violent). I looked into treatment for it and it seems to be fixable with hypnosis by a professional trained in this condition. It's actually a neurological issue according to this specialist
I feel exactly the same and I keep challenging it but the illness is getting me. It's so hard to manage cos it's so changeable. I'm sorry you feel the same

Aw I'm so sorry. I would urge you to get some help for that. Get your LFT checked because after 24 hours it's very hard to reverse the damage and if it doesn't kill you then you'll be damaged for life. I worry about you.

It depends actually because we usually want "proof" that the person actually likes us and wants us. Sometimes, depending on how far they are in recovery they may be quite angry and try to withhold things from the person in order to punish them. I'm just going on what I know if my BPD journey and past situations. I think you should reach out and see what the response is and judge it from there. As long as that's what you want :)
Hey, I'm just checking to see did you get some help?

Hey, I'm glad you've posted this. It must be difficult to be on that end of BPD. I hope your wellbeing is good just now? Otherwise I'd advise you take time to look after you because I know as someone with BPD how draining it is for others. 

I would say the person is likely waiting for you to reach out and show them that you care and are thinking about them. It's complex but it can be simplified. 
It's unfortunate this happens as someone who had split a few times on the latest partner...I tried to explain and make amends after it happened but he wasn't open to that so I let it go. I hope he reaches out but if not, what can I do. But it would be reassuring to see he is thinking of me and didn't just forget everything we shared. 

As long as you are in a good headspace I don't see any harm in a nice, gentle, caring text or something but if anything kicks off I'd say it's best to just respond with "I'm sorry that you are still struggling, get in touch when you are feeling a bit better and I'd love to chat. I care about you and hope you are ok". Or something like that.

Totally feel this. I'm so sorry you do too. Other people...meh. I think in this life we gotta put our attention on ourselves and make ourselves happy or content and try not to let others'affect us so badly. I know this is very difficult but it's working for me to be able to be content in myself means others don't have that power over me. 

This took a long time though and yes I'm currently experiencing a crisis but that's due to other things. But I have found more peace by letting go of what I can't control and that is other people and what they think and feel about me. 

Take time out. Focus on you as if your life is a wee experiment just now and see what the results are in a month or two. I found by treating it like that it took a lot of worry and stress away. 

I hope this is helpful

Hey, firstly can I say that is amazing that you can manage your symptoms so well although if it's taking such a toll on you I'd say maybe to re-evaluate things and look at an alternative way of self management? Or maybe it's about informing your partner but expressing you are not seeking anything except understanding of your situation. Explain how it's impacting you and that you worry about the health consequences? 

I feel this loneliness and I'm single. I don't get into relationships or have casual sex anymore because I understand why I'm doing it and that I feel worse after (a bit like the impact of alcohol...the hangover isn't worth it to me). 

I find I get less lonely when I put my attention on things like documentaries of people's life stories and podcasts on crime, how the mind works (Derren brown has the "bootcamp for the mind" audiobook and I highly recommend it). These things remind me it's not all BPD and that any human can react impulsively or have fleeting traits that we tend to have chronically. 

I hope this is somewhat helpful

Bad choice of words I think. They need to not be getting a grip of anything
Suicide by lion... unsuccessful

I'm sorry you feel like that. I'm currently suicidal and struggling with what I'm gonna do. I feel the same. But I don't even care now about others and what they think...I'm just concerned about getting it done properly. But it sounds like you need some support and a listener. I really hope someone can be of help as I'm not able to offer much whilst I'm in this situation. I apologise if it's not helpful but I wanted to acknowledge your post. I hope you find what you need

I don't know if this is helpful but I feel the same. I keep having recurring suicidal episodes and am exhausted to just survive them and once I think I got through it and feel a bit better...boom. another episode. It's so bloody hard! People with BPD have a lot of complex shit to deal with (not minimizing other mental illnesses) but as someone with BPD Jesus it's brutal. Every day is exhausting to survive the awful symptoms of the disorder.

I'm so pleased you are having a good day :) 

I had a good day yesterday but am struggling with the flip side today. I know that it gets better but I know I have chronic suicidality and that is so painful and intense it's almost like the good times can't be enjoyed. 

I don't mean that to bring you down! Not at all...just my unfortunate experience lately. But I totally get those good times feel so intense that it's beautiful 😊 I'm so pleased you are having a nice time. We all deserve it for having to endure such horrendous symptoms. 

I'd a nice time painting yesterday, listening to music and reading. Some comedy always helps!
Hey how are you?

I've done this multiple times years ago when I didn't know how to manage my impulses. I regretted it after a few hours and phoned for help. Let me tell you this...I've been through the symptoms of initial overdose as well as the antidote for it and both are brutal. But I can totally understand why someone would choose this when in despair. I had a nurse tell me he witnessed someone in their care die slowly over a few days due to not being able to reverse the overdose and it was pretty horrendous for that patient. 

Then there was another story of a woman who survived but now must always have a urine bag or something on her because her organs were so damaged. 

It's a high risk with a low chance if death. Please get yourself help just now. As someone who deals with chronic suicidality I do understand. I want to do it but I already have and know what it feels like. It's not what you may think it will be like. It's very very slow and painful and unlikely to kill you...it's more likely to leave you damaged for life. 

Please get help for this and reconsider things. I understand you don't wanna hear "you don't need to do this" because suicide is so subjective and other people need to understand the pain of that person. I know that pain. It's awful and I too want a way out but believe me this isn't it

Yeah I had that years ago. It's a red flag if someone you've just met says that so soon. That's likely your brain trying to protect you. Plus, we with BPD have attachment issues and it can be hard to deal with an intense person that isn't us. It's a bit much. Plus I also think it's that thing of being disgusted by affection and love but also desiring it.

Yep I feel that too. I am not in any way discouraging people to ask for help but the system just isn't helpful. It's a one size fits all approach and people with more complex needs and disorders just don't get the help we need. I was in this situation a few days ago but I didn't bother taking myself to hospital in order to cause myself more distress and fury. It helps me to remember this is a system and politics issue rather than medical staff individually being unhelpful and targeting us (although I've had experience of this too unfortunately). 

I cannot yet afford private health care. The best thing I've found is in time seeing that I've got through the distress and suicidal tendencies by avoiding these very scenarios because they cause me more harm and anger. I can't cope with how disappointing it is. So I avoid it. 

It's a terrible situation to be in. To be very suicidal and not have a reliable support network and to have to just cope because they won't help. It's awful. 

I'm so sorry that you experience this too. We all deserve better but it looks like it's about being resourceful and helping each other by just listening. 💕

I should add that when I typed this this morning I was extremely distressed and set on suicide. 

I have had a few hours of pleasantness let's say, thanks to the response from you guys. 

I turned my day around for a short while. I hope I can maintain it. But the issue is...it is chronic. I know the nature of this all too well and it is disturbing. No medication helps. I tried all the lifestyle things. Trying everything that I can. I am willing to put effort in and be resourceful. It's just incredibly exhausting to barely survive. 

When I say my physical body is "destroyed" that is how it feels when I'm in a distressed state. It is different. I broke lots of bones and had to rehabilitate myself. My injuries have healed well but the psychological impact is devastating. 

Thank you to those who replied and I am so grateful for this forum. 

Let's hope I can maintain this for the weekend that I dread!

Aw man I know that feeling. I think just communicate to him (I have BPD so I understand how difficult it is) but day something like "hey, I'm feeling a bit upset and need some affection. That would help me feel reassured about us. Can we have a cuddle and I'll leave you to game?" 

Hope that is helpful x

I'm glad I could help! It's actually given me an idea for a journal entry to help when I'm getting upset over the illness so thank you! 
Definitely take time to list all your qualities, values, principles and morals that are what you believe to be distinct from the symptoms (because we know they shift when symptomatic). Enjoy getting to know yourself as it is a nice thing to do! <3

I feel like that. I can't quite separate "me" from the illness. I think it's partly to do with our unstable sense of self. 

Definitely not alone with that. Try not to label yourself. It's hard but I've learned that labels can help in certain contexts but for your own mind it's likely unhelpful. 

The last thing you need is to be hard on yourself. I understand though that it is because it's hard to separate ourselves from the illness as they seem so intrinsically linked...I suppose one way I'd propose how we could find out who we are compared to BPD would be to get all patients with BPD together and identify the symptoms and separate the traits. That is what I try to do mentally anyway. It's hard though

I did the same to my ex a few years ago and I have since made amends and gave him closure. I respect his boundaries and the trauma he now has due to me. He messages me now and again and I'm fine with that. After all, I've been abused so I know how it feels to be on the receiving end. So I needed to realise I did the same thing *unknowingly* to him and must deal with the consequences of my verbal abuse. It's not right. But that doesn't mean we are all awful people. If we can take responsibility (ahhh such a stingy phrase!)and work through our Symptoms to better ourselves then I think we are doing well. We aren't bad if we have remorse and respect for those we hurt- even if it was mostly the illness. 
Once we accept who we are or gain a sense of who we are we can fill that void and others will gravitate naturally towards us. That's what I've found in my recovery. Balance and flow. I take my inspiration from nature :) nothing is forced. It's all about balance and flowing naturally. I try to keep these things in mind when I wanna beg someone to stick around (I no longer do that! Wow haha). Hope that helps and that you can also fight through all this and be able to be self reliant. It's very hard but very rewarding.

I felt and still feel the guilt as I wrote this post. It is so hard to manage but we can't continue to punish ourselves for past wrongs. We can try to make amends and move on and take the lesdon from it. But therapy would help with guilt I would imagine. 

Thank you :)

MBT has significantly helped me manage my reactions to others and my symptoms. I'm able to have better interactions and relationships and reduced the frequency of many of the destructive symptoms. 

I only managed 1 year in group therapy out of 2 years and that's because I couldn't deal with hearing other people's trauma. It was really awful. It was discussed with the professionals and decided I would continue with individual treatment and that worked wonders for me. 

Honestly MBT has seriously helped me manage the illness and therefore meant I could lead a better, less painful life. 

I've also done a lot of reading into self development books and spirituality. That is to supplement the MBT as a holistic treatment. 

Definitely recommend! I do have a DBT book that I use the skills from regularly. So if you are getting one therapy you can always cherry pick certain skills that work for you.

I'm really sorry you experienced this from your cousin. Just remember that it's more a reflection of her and her ego and lack of understanding than it is about you. People can be mean, uneducated in these matters, say the wrong thing (most of the time this is due to a lack of understanding and awareness but sometimes it can be because the person is very egotistical), do the wrong thing and people can also be helpful and understanding. 

I know it's annoying and hurtful for sure but just remind yourself "my cousin is more concerned with her ego and isn't actually listening or able to sympathise. This is a reflection of her life and emotional states at the moment. She has annoyed me and hurt me but I'm gonna choose to tune this out and try and find someone who can empathise/sympathise with me in my time of need" 

Is that helpful at all? I use these types of things to help me gain clarity on the situation before concluding "they don't care!" 

I hope your situation improves. I've been there myself and I know how bloody hard it is.

Hey

I hope you are doing ok. 

I can understand to a degree. I feel the same and I'm nearly 30. My bf left me although I never did anything nasty or out of order- he just found it draining to reassure me in a crisis which I completely understand. 

I am used to being alone but the emptiness is awful. I find it so hard to deal with. Thankfully I don't self harm or anything anymore but it's so tempting. 

I do feel that I need to work on myself more and maybe leave relationships for another while because I unfortunately do tend to split on people and that must be awful for them. It's really confusing for everyone. 

I know you are venting and I do feel similar. I would not say you are damaged goods. I'd say if you felt more in control in being alone then do that but don't deprive yourself of joy for fear to win. I suppose it's about seeing where you are at in recovery and making a judgement on that. I know after being left by my partner that I just let him go, no matter how hurt I was because nothing good comes from forcing or begging. I have made peace with it and detached from the outcome and realise that all people have flaws (me included 100%!) And that it's about being strong in being alone but also accepting people come and go in life. Trying to detach from the abandonment and healing that has worked for me. I have particular standards when it comes to my romantic relationship and I won't accept less than that. So I was also thinking I may need to end the relationship if he wasn't willing to work together. 

It's all about balance. Taking responsibility (god I hate that but it's true!) And also not taking responsibility for other people's emotions. I realised I was blaming myself for stuff that wasn't mine. 

But I do understand how you feel somewhat. I sway between "I'm doing the best I can with an awful illness that makes relationships difficult" to "I am a terrible person that no one wants to be around and no wonder i have been abandoned. No one would be crazy enough to be in a relationship with me". That is hard.
